<page>
 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2023-CV-0044
 Lindsey Walker, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Lindsey Walker
Date:
January 9, 2024
Location:
Offices of Carter & Smith Injury Lawyers
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Carlos Fox, Carter & Smith Injury Lawyers
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but I can confirm I'm the plaintiff in this case.
Q: Fair enough. Let's talk about the collision. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Houston, Texas, on a weekday afternoon. I had a green light heading east.
Q: What happened as you entered the intersection?
A: A vehicle coming from the north ran through its red light and struck the driver's side of my car. It was a side impact. My car
spun partway around and came to rest against the curb.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?
A: Not really. I heard brakes at the last second and then the impact. There was no time to react.
Q: Were you able to get out of your car on your own?
A: Yes, but I was shaking and my right arm hurt badly. Someone nearby helped me sit on the sidewalk until the paramedics
arrived.
Q: Did you go to a hospital that day?
A: Yes. They X-rayed my shoulder and checked my neck. The emergency room doctor said nothing was broken, but he told me
the shoulder was seriously strained and wrapped it in a sling.
Q: After that, what treatment did you receive for the shoulder?
A: I was referred to an orthopedic clinic. I went to physical therapy about three times a week for several months. I also had a
series of injections, and the doctor discussed whether I might need surgery if the pain didn't improve.
Q: Are you still receiving treatment?
A: Yes, I still do home exercises every day and I see my physical therapist less often now. Some days the shoulder is much better,
and other days it aches a lot.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: It's made ordinary things difficult. I can't lift heavy grocery bags with my right hand, and I have trouble reaching into the
upper cabinets. I used to play recreational softball on weekends, and I have not been able to play since the accident.
Q: Has it affected your work?
A: I work in an office, so I can type, but I've had to take some time off for appointments and I avoid tasks that require lifting
boxes. My supervisor has been understanding about it.
Q: Do you sleep normally?
A: Not really. I often wake up at night when I roll onto my right side. I've been using extra pillows to support the arm.
</page>
